# Benchmarks

<!-- Generated by `bazel run //:r7rs -- bench-report`: don't edit by hand. -->

ecraven's R7RS benchmarks (`bench/r7rs-ecraven/`, the set behind <https://ecraven.github.io/r7rs-benchmarks/>) on this implementation and on the other R7RS implementations in `nix develop .#bench`, each run with its own prelude and postlude and as ecraven's `bench` script runs it, so the numbers compare with his tables. How to run it, and what is measured: `bench/README.md`.

## Conditions

- Run by `bazel run //:r7rs -- bench-report --scale 0.1 --interpreter-timeout 60 --native /private/var/tmp/_bazel_anon/c39da747b4f1beec5c6df9262d584a7f/execroot/_main/bazel-out/darwin_arm64-fastbuild/bin/scheme-native --note 'The maintainer'"'"'s 16-core machine, shared with other agents'"'"' builds and benchmarks (the load averages below): differences under 2x are within the noise. bench/thresholds.json is measured separately, by bench-check (bench/README.md).'`, at commit `459e380bf32b`, from 2026-11-18 12:14 UTC, for 86.3 minutes.
- Host: Darwin 27.0.0 (arm64), Apple M3 Max, 16 CPUs, 128 GB of memory.
- The maintainer's 16-core machine, shared with other agents' builds and benchmarks (the load averages below): differences under 2x are within the noise. bench/thresholds.json is measured separately, by bench-check (bench/README.md).
- Counts: 0.1 times each program's own count (at least 1), on every implementation; the Count column gives it.
- Ours, interpreter: run 0.1 times that count (at least 1), its time then scaled up to the count the others ran, marked †.
- Ours, JIT: one JVM runs the harness 3 times. The first, in a fresh process, is the comparable number (as for every other implementation, and in ecraven's tables: the harness's own timing, startup excluded); "JIT steady" is the best of the others, once the JIT has compiled the program.
- Ours, native: the native launcher (`bazel build //:scheme-native`, which keeps the Graal JIT) runs the harness 3 times in one process, as our JIT's JVM does: the first is the comparable number, "native steady" the best of the others. "Native with startup" is the first with the process's startup and exit: its wall time, less the iterations after the first.
- A run is killed after 300 s (ecraven's `CPU_LIMIT`), our JIT's and native launcher's after that once per iteration, our interpreter's after 60 s. Peak memory is the process's maximum resident set size. Our JVMs and native launcher run with `-Xmx2g`, a fixed maximum heap (bench/README.md "Heap"); the memory tables also give how much of their heap the program used (Peak memory).
- The machine's 1-minute load average: 6.74 at the start, at most 12.37 before a program, 9.29 at the end.

Maximum resident set size in MB, failed runs included (our JIT's and native launcher's over all its iterations).

For ours, how much of that is heap the program used, in MB (bench/README.md "Heap"):

- live: the most the program kept alive, measured by collecting the whole heap every 0.5 s in another run of the program, whose times aren't used ("too short": it ended before the first);
- after GC: the most the heap held right after a collection in the timed run, from the JVM's GC log (the native launcher's: its `-XX:+PrintGC` lines): what was live, and the garbage the collection left in the old generation ("no GC": no collection).
- The native launcher has no live heap: native-image has no `jcmd` to collect and count it from outside.

## Failures

A timeout is a run killed at its limit (Conditions); our interpreter's limit may be shorter than the others', so its timeouts say only that it took longer than that.

## How each implementation ran

`{src}` is the program as the bench script builds it, `{input}` its `.input` file (with the count above).

- Ours, JIT: `java -XX:+UseSerialGC -XX:CICompilerCount=4 -Xmx2g -Xlog:gc:file={gc.log} (Graal JIT, background compilation) -m scheme.launcher/scheme.launcher.SchemeMain {src} < {input}`. With `bench/postlude.scm` as the postlude.
- Ours, native: `scheme-native --vm.Xmx2g --vm.XX:+PrintGC {src} < {input}`. With `bench/postlude.scm` as the postlude.
- Ours, interpreter: `java -XX:+UseSerialGC -XX:CICompilerCount=4 -Xmx2g -Dpolyglot.engine.AllowExperimentalOptions=true -Dpolyglot.engine.Compilation=false -Xlog:gc:file={gc.log} -m scheme.launcher/scheme.launcher.SchemeMain {src} < {input}`. With `bench/postlude.scm` as the postlude.
- Chez: `scheme --optimize-level 2 --compile-imported-libraries --libdirs {chezlibs} --program {src} < {input}`. With `Chez-postlude.scm`; ecraven/chez-scheme-libraries, patched: base.sls: vector-append vector-copy!.
- Racket: `raco make {src} && racket {src} < {input}`. With `Racket-prelude.scm`; the r7rs package (lexi-lambda/racket-r7rs, r7rs-lib).
- Chicken: `csc -R r7rs -X r7rs -block -O3 -C -O3 -d0 {src} -o {exe} && {exe} < {input}`. With `Chicken-prelude.scm`.
- Guile: `guild compile -O3 {src} && guile {src} < {input}`. With `Guile-prelude.scm`.
- Gauche: `gosh -r7 -b {src} < {input}`. With `Gauche-postlude.scm`; SLIB 3b7.
- Chibi: `chibi-scheme -m scheme.load -e (load "{src}") < {input}`. With `Chibi-prelude.scm` and `Chibi-postlude.scm`.
